Physics: Coverage is well balanced across mechanics, electromagnetism, optics, thermal physics and modern physics, and almost all items are clean, single- or double-step calculations suited to the 90 s BITSAT budget (keys verified correct except q37). The essential fixes are the reversed angular-momentum key in q37 and the missing q29, plus small unit/wording repairs in q25, q26 and q28. A couple of items (q12's off-axis-source fringe count and q30's cavity superposition) sit at the upper end of the level and are the most time-costly, so keep at most one such multi-step item in the section.

[minor] With the central maximum shifted to y = −1.6 mm and β = 1.6 mm, bright fringes fall exactly on both screen edges (y = ±8.0 mm), so the count depends on whether boundary maxima are included (11 vs 9); shift the screen limits (e.g. ±7.5 mm) off the maxima and adjust the key.
[minor] The stem asks for the reading in kg wt but all options are labelled "kg"; label the options kg wt (or ask for the reading in newtons) so the units are consistent.

[minor] "Placed exactly along one side of the triangle, parallel to it" is self-contradictory (coincident versus merely parallel); state plainly that the straight wire coincides with that side, carrying current in the same sense.

[minor] The data imply Y ≈ 4×10^8 Pa and strains of 2–10%, which contradicts "metal wire loaded within its elastic limit"; rescale the loads/area so the elongations are millimetre-scale and Y ~10^11 Pa.
[major] Question 29 is absent (numbering jumps from 28 to 30), so the section carries only 39 items and must be completed or renumbered before printing.
[major] The key is wrong: conservation of angular momentum gives ω = (6×3)/2 = 9 rad s⁻¹, i.e. option D, whereas the keyed option A (1 rad s⁻¹) violates I₁ω₁ = I₂ω₂.

Chemistry: The section covers physical, inorganic and organic chemistry broadly and all numerical keys (46, 53, 54, 59, 64, 75) check out, with most items comfortably solvable within 90 s. Balance is slightly skewed towards alcohols/phenols/ethers (44, 48, 60) and magnetism (45, 66, 77), while aromaticity is tested twice (76, 80) and a few items are bare recall (42, 47, 61). Swapping the redundant aromaticity and Williamson items for syllabus-aligned topics such as ionic-equilibrium calculations or p-block/solid-state reasoning would tighten the paper.
[minor] The 18-electron (EAN) rule applied to metallocenes is outside the BITSAT/NCERT scope for coordination compounds, so the item rewards out-of-syllabus recall rather than syllabus reasoning.
[minor] This tests the same Williamson ether-synthesis idea as q44 (choose the alkoxide/phenoxide–halide pair), so one of the two should be replaced to avoid conceptual repetition.

[minor] Distractor B differs from the key only in using the obsolete 'dichloro' instead of 'dichlorido', which is defensible under older IUPAC usage; replace it with an unambiguously wrong name (e.g. wrong oxidation state or wrong cation/anion order).

[minor] Key D is only tenable if the figure shows a molecule carrying both an α-hydrogen-free –CHO and a CH3CO– (or CH3CH(OH)–) group, e.g. 4-acetylbenzaldehyde; for a simple aldehyde such as benzaldehyde statement (iii) is false and no listed option is correct.

[minor] Since NH3 is conventionally taught as a strong-field ligand, the low-spin d7 answer 1.73 BM (option A) is arguably defensible at this level, so the stem should state that [Co(NH3)6]2+ is high-spin (or use a clearly weak-field ligand).
[major] This duplicates q76 almost exactly (Hückel aromaticity of the same small-ring cations/anions, with cyclopentadienyl cation appearing in both), so it must be replaced by a different topic.

English Proficiency: The section covers the expected BITSAT spread — vocabulary in context, synonyms/antonym, idiom, grammar and error spotting, jumbles and a short RC pair — and the level is broadly appropriate, with Q91 and Q92 sitting at the easy end and Q87 testing nothing as printed. The balance is slightly grammar-heavy (four error/preposition items) and carries two very similar chronological narrative jumbles plus two adjective-synonym items, so replacing one jumble with a sentence-improvement or one-word-substitution item would widen the skill coverage. Before printing, also clean the duplicated option letters ("(A) (A)") in most items and the option block repeated twice in Q84.

[minor] The item is tagged "Sentence Completion (vocabulary)" but is actually a word-analogy (NURSE : HOSPITAL) of the kind used in the reasoning section, so the label/instruction must be corrected or the item replaced with a genuine completion item.

[minor] The stem claims the parts are "marked (A), (B), (C) and (D)", but the sentence only has slashes and the four options are printed as empty labels, so the part text (or A–D markers in the sentence) must be supplied.

[major] The key P–Q–R is the order in which the sentences are already printed, so no rearrangement is actually tested (and the narrative-chronology jumble duplicates Q82); relabel the parts so the correct sequence is scrambled.
[minor] Tagged "Error Spotting / Sentence Improvement" although it is a preposition fill-in-the-blank with no error to spot; retag it as grammar/sentence completion.

Logical Reasoning: The section covers the expected BITSAT logical-reasoning spread (analogy, classification, blood relations, coding, series, syllogism, figural items) and the keys that can be checked are all correct, including the +4/+6/+8/+10/+12 number pattern in q104. The level is on the easy side, with several 20–30 second items (q97, q100) and no genuinely demanding analytical or seating/arrangement puzzle to stretch the top end. Before printing, restore the missing artwork for q99 (and confirm the figure/options for q101 and q103 render), strip the duplicated option labels seen in q96/q100/q102 and the repeated option block in q105, and swap one of the two identical alphabet-shift items.
[major] The item is unanswerable as printed: no figure is attached and all four options are blank, so the odd-figure-out cannot be identified or the key A verified.
[minor] The four answer options are printed twice in identical blocks; delete the duplicated set (the key B itself is correct).
[minor] This duplicates the mechanic of q96 (a fixed forward alphabet shift, +3 here versus +5 there), so one of the two should be replaced by a different coding rule or a non-shift analogy.
[minor] The item is tagged "Word Formation / Dictionary Order" but actually tests a meaningful logical sequence, so the category label should be corrected (content and key A are fine).

Mathematics: All 44 supplied keys check out on recomputation, and the spread across calculus, algebra, coordinate geometry, vectors/3D, probability and statistics is broadly appropriate, though Integral Calculus is slightly over-weighted (five items) and the perpendicular-foot technique appears twice. The level is mostly single-concept NCERT-standard and a touch easy overall, with only q115, q119, q126, q132 and q149 demanding genuine multi-step work within the 90-second budget. The section cannot be printed as-is because item 146 is missing, and a few presentation/difficulty fixes are needed.
[major] Question 146 is absent from the section (numbering jumps from 145 to 147), leaving only 44 items where 45 are required.
[minor] The determinant is typeset as three separate barred rows |1+a 1 1| |1 1+b 1| |1 1 1+c|, which reads like a product of moduli; display it as a single 3×3 determinant.
[minor] This tests essentially the same perpendicular-foot formula as q113 (image = 2×foot − point), so replace one of the two with a different coordinate-geometry concept.
[minor] A single direct substitution into n(A∪B)=n(A)+n(B)−n(A∩B) is too trivial for BITSAT; make it a two-step set/counting problem.
